        customer_id,
        strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS year_month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN txn_amount > 0 THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_deposits,

    FROM customer_monthly_balance

WITH cohort AS (
    SELECT
        legislator_id,
        MIN(start_date) AS first_term_start
    FROM legislators_terms
    WHERE start_date BETWEEN '1917-01-01' AND '1999-12-31'
    GROUP BY legislator_id
),
years AS (
    SELECT generate_series(1, 20) AS year_after_start
),
cohort_size AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM cohort
),
retention AS (
    SELECT
        y.year_after_start,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ct.legislator_id) AS retained_count
    FROM years y
    CROSS JOIN cohort ct
    JOIN legislators_terms lt ON ct.legislator_id = lt.legislator_id
    WHERE DATE(lt.start_date) <= DATE(ct.first_term_start, '+' || y.year_after_start || ' years', '-1 day')
      AND DATE(lt.end_date) > DATE(ct.first_term_start, '+' || y.year_after_start || ' years', '-1 day')
    GROUP BY y.year_after_start
)
SELECT
    y.year_after_start,
    COALESCE(r.retained_count, 0) * 1.0 / cs.total AS retention_rate
FROM years y
LEFT JOIN retention r ON y.year_after_start = r.year_after_start
CROSS JOIN cohort_size cs
ORDER BY y.year_after_start;
```

WITH base_orders AS (
  SELECT
    pco.row_id,
    pco.order_id,
    pco.customer_id,
    CASE WHEN pco.pizza_id = 1 THEN 'Meatlovers' ELSE 'Other' END AS pizza_name,
    pco.pizza_id,
    pco.order_time
  FROM pizza_customer_orders pco
),
std_toppings AS (
  SELECT
    pr.pizza_id,
    tt.topping_name
  FROM pizza_recipes pr
  JOIN pizza_toppings tt ON pr.topping_id = tt.topping_id
),
excluded_toppings AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    pge.row_id,
    pte.topping_name
  FROM pizza_get_exclusions pge
  JOIN pizza_toppings pte ON pge.topping_id = pte.topping_id
),
extra_toppings AS (
  SELECT 
    pge.row_id,
    pte.topping_name
  FROM pizza_get_extras pge
  JOIN pizza_toppings pte ON pge.topping_id = pte.topping_id
),
all_ingredients AS (
  SELECT
    bo.row_id,
    bo.order_id,
    bo.customer_id,
    bo.pizza_name,
    COALESCE(prst.topping_name, '') AS topping_name,
    'standard' AS source
  FROM base_orders bo
  LEFT JOIN std_toppings prst ON bo.pizza_id = prst.pizza_id
  WHERE bo.pizza_name IS NOT NULL
),
ingredients_excluded_removed AS (
  SELECT
    ai.row_id,
    ai.order_id,
    ai.customer_id,
    ai.pizza_name,
    ai.topping_name
  FROM all_ingredients ai
  LEFT JOIN excluded_toppings et ON ai.row_id = et.row_id AND ai.topping_name = et.topping_name
  WHERE et.topping_name IS NULL AND ai.topping_name != ''
),
ingredients_with_extra AS (
  SELECT
    ier.row_id,
    ier.order_id,
    ier.customer_id,
    ier.pizza_name,
    ier.topping_name
  FROM ingredients_excluded_removed ier
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    xe.row_id,
    xe.row_id AS order_id,
    NULL as customer_id,
    bo.pizza_name,
    xe.topping_name
  FROM extra_toppings xe
  JOIN base_orders bo ON xe.row_id = bo.row_id
),
ingredients_final AS (
  SELECT
    row_id,
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    pizza_name,
    topping_name,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM ingredients_with_extra
  GROUP BY row_id, order_id, customer_id, pizza_name, topping_name
),
ingredients_ordered AS (
  SELECT
    row_id,
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    pizza_name,
    CASE 
      WHEN cnt > 1 THEN '2x' || topping_name 
      ELSE topping_name 
    END AS topping_name_display,
    cnt
  FROM ingredients_final
),
ingredients_sorted AS (
  SELECT
    row_id,
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    pizza_name,
    topping_name_display,
    cnt
  FROM ingredients_ordered
),
ingredients_agg AS (
  SELECT
    row_id,
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    pizza_name,
    -- first list toppings with count>1 in alphabetical order, then single-count toppings alphabetically
    GROUP_CONCAT(topping_name_display, ', ') AS ingredients_str
  FROM (
    SELECT
      row_id,
      order_id,
      customer_id,
      pizza_name,
      topping_name_display,
      cnt
    FROM ingredients_sorted
    ORDER BY
      row_id,
      -- ordering by count desc (so 2x first) and alphabetically
      CASE WHEN cnt > 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
      topping_name_display
  )
  GROUP BY row_id, order_id, customer_id, pizza_name
)
SELECT
  ia.row_id,
  ia.order_id,
  ia.customer_id,
  ia.pizza_name,
  ia.pizza_name || ': ' || ia.ingredients_str AS final_ingredients
FROM ingredients_agg ia
ORDER BY ia.row_id ASC
;
```

WITH filtered_events AS (

    GROUP BY product_id

adds AS (

leaves AS (

    WHERE event_type = 'leave_without_purchase'
    GROUP BY product_id
),
purchases AS (
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS purchase_count
    FROM filtered_events
    WHERE event_type = 'purchase'
    GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(v.product_id, a.product_id, l.product_id, p.product_id) AS product_id,
    COALESCE(view_count, 0) AS view_count,
    COALESCE(add_count, 0) AS add_count,
    COALESCE(leave_count, 0) AS leave_count,
    COALESCE(purchase_count, 0) AS purchase_count
FROM views v
FULL OUTER JOIN adds a ON v.product_id = a.product_id
FULL OUTER JOIN leaves l ON COALESCE(v.product_id, a.product_id) = l.product_id
FULL OUTER JOIN purchases p ON COALESCE(v.product_id, a.product_id, l.product_id) = p.product_id

    FROM film f
    JOIN language l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
    JOIN film_category fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
    WHERE l.name = 'English'
      AND c.name = 'Children'
      AND (f.rating = 'G' OR f.rating = 'PG')
      AND f.length <= 120
      AND f.release_year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
), ActorFilmCounts AS (
    SELECT fa.actor_id, COUNT(*) AS film_count
    FROM film_actor fa
    JOIN EligibleFilms ef ON fa.film_id = ef.film_id
    GROUP BY fa.actor_id
)
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM ActorFilmCounts afc
JOIN actor a ON afc.actor_id = a.actor_id
ORDER BY afc.film_count DESC
LIMIT 1;

    o.customer_id,
    o.order_id,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp,

  FROM delivered_orders

recency_rank AS (

    customer_id,
    last_purchase,
    JULIANDAY(MAX(last_purchase) OVER()) - JULIANDAY(last_purchase) AS recency_days
  FROM recency_calc
),
recency_score AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    last_purchase,
    recency_days,
    NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY recency_days) AS recency
  FROM recency_rank
),
frequency_calc AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    COUNT(order_id) AS frequency
  FROM delivered_orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
frequency_score AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    frequency,
    NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS frequency_score
  FROM frequency_calc
),
monetary_calc AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    SUM(payment_value) AS monetary
  FROM delivered_orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
monetary_score AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    monetary,
    NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY monetary DESC) AS monetary_score
  FROM monetary_calc
),
rfm AS (
  SELECT 
    r.customer_id,
    r.recency,
    f.frequency_score AS frequency,
    m.monetary_score AS monetary,
    (f.frequency_score + m.monetary_score) AS freq_monetary_sum
  FROM recency_score r
  JOIN frequency_score f ON r.customer_id = f.customer_id
  JOIN monetary_score m ON r.customer_id = m.customer_id
),
rfm_segments AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    recency,
    frequency,
    monetary,
    freq_monetary_sum,
    CASE
      WHEN recency = 1 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Champions'
      WHEN recency IN (4,5) AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 'Can''t Lose Them'
      WHEN recency IN (4,5) AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 3 AND 6 THEN 'Hibernating'
      WHEN recency IN (4,5) AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'Lost'
      WHEN recency IN (2,3) AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Loyal Customers'
      WHEN recency = 3 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 5 AND 6 THEN 'Needs Attention'
      WHEN recency = 1 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 7 AND 8 THEN 'Recent Users'
      WHEN (recency = 1 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 5 AND 6) OR (recency = 2 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 5 AND 8) THEN 'Potential Loyalists'
      WHEN recency = 1 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Price Sensitive'
      WHEN recency = 2 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Promising'
      WHEN recency = 3 AND freq_monetary_sum BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'About to Sleep'
      ELSE 'Others'
    END AS rfm_segment
  FROM rfm
),
avg_sales AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    SUM(payment_value) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS avg_sale_per_order
  FROM delivered_orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
)

SELECT
  s.rfm_segment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id) AS num_customers,
  AVG(a.avg_sale_per_order) AS avg_sale_per_order
FROM rfm_segments s
JOIN avg_sales a ON s.customer_id = a.customer_id
GROUP BY s.rfm_segment
ORDER BY avg_sale_per_order DESC
LIMIT 1000;

Provided benchmark documentation:
# Introduction to the RFM Model

The RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) model segments and scores customers based on three key dimensions:

• Recency (R): How long it has been since the customer’s last purchase. A lower R score (e.g., R = 1) indicates a very recent purchase, while a higher R score (e.g., R = 5) indicates a longer time since the last purchase.

• Frequency (F): How often the customer purchases within a given time period. A lower F score (e.g., F = 1) signifies that the customer buys very frequently, whereas a higher F score (e.g., F = 5) indicates less frequent purchasing.

• Monetary (M): The total amount of money the customer spends. A lower M score (e.g., M = 1) indicates higher overall spending, while a higher M score (e.g., M = 5) signifies lower spending over the measured period.

Each customer’s R, F, and M scores are determined by their respective percentiles when compared to other customers. By concatenating the three scores, you get an “RFM cell”—for instance, a customer with R=1, F=5, and M=2 would fall into the 152 segment.

# RFM Segmentation Calculation

After scoring customers on Recency, Frequency, and Monetary values, the next step is to group them into segments that require different marketing or sales strategies. Typically:

1. Determine each customer’s recency score (R) from 1 to 5 (1 = very recent purchase, 5 = not recent).  
2. Determine each customer’s frequency score (F) from 1 to 5 (1 = most frequent purchases, 5 = least frequent).  
3. Determine each customer’s monetary score (M) from 1 to 5 (1 = highest spending, 5 = lowest spending).  
4. Concatenate these three scores into an RFM score (e.g., 153, 514).

By analyzing the distribution of RFM scores and placing them into buckets—for example, “Champions,” “Loyal Customers,” “At Risk,” “Lost,” etc.—you can tailor marketing, sales, and retention strategies to maximize the potential of each segment. 

For instance, a “Champion” (R=1, F=1, M=1) is a recent, frequent, and high-spending user who is highly valuable to your business, whereas a “Lost” customer (e.g., R=5, F=5, M=5) may require re-engagement offers or might no longer be cost-effective to target. Different segments can thus be prioritized based on their profitability and likelihood of responding positively to marketing efforts.

## RFM Segmentation Logic

Customers are assigned to specific segments (RFM Buckets) based on a combination of their Recency, Frequency, and Monetary scores. The segmentation logic is as follows:

- **Champions**: Customers who have made a recent purchase, with high frequency and high monetary value. These are considered the most valuable customers.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 4.

- **Can't Lose Them**: Previously frequent and high-spending customers who have not made a recent purchase. These customers are at risk of leaving and need attention.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 2.

- **Hibernating**: Customers whose last purchase was a while ago, with low to moderate frequency and spending. These customers might have lost interest in the products.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 3 and 6.

- **Lost**: Customers who have not purchased in a long time and have low frequency and monetary value. These customers are likely lost.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 10.

- **Loyal Customers**: Customers who are frequent buyers with decent spending levels, and they have made a purchase relatively recently. These customers are likely to be very loyal.
  - Criteria: Recency = 2 or 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 4.

- **Needs Attention**: Customers whose purchase frequency and spending are moderate. They haven't bought very recently, but they could be incentivized to become more active.
  - Criteria: Recency = 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 6.

- **Recent Users**: Customers who made a purchase recently, but their frequency and spending are moderate. These are relatively new or inconsistent buyers.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 8.

- **Potential Loyalists**: Customers who show potential to become loyal customers. They have good frequency and monetary scores, and they have made recent purchases. With the right engagement, they could become loyal customers.
  - Criteria:
    - Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 6.
    - OR Recency = 2 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 8.

- **Price Sensitive**: Customers who have made recent purchases but tend to spend less, indicating they may be more sensitive to price.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 9 and 10.

- **Promising**: These customers exhibit high potential with decent frequency and monetary scores, and they could become more valuable over time.
  - Criteria: Recency = 2 and Frequency + Monetary score between 9 and 10.

- **About to Sleep**: Customers whose frequency and spending are low, and their last purchase was some time ago. These customers are likely to become inactive.
  - Criteria: Recency = 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 10.

## Summary

This segmentation logic groups customers based on their behavior in terms of when they last purchased (Recency), how often they purchase (Frequency), and how much they spend (Monetary). By understanding which group a customer belongs to, organizations can tailor marketing strategies to engage the right audience more effectively, improving customer retention and maximizing value.

WITH month_indices AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT mth FROM monthly_sales
  WHERE mth >= '2016-01-01'
  ORDER BY mth
),
numbered_months AS (
  SELECT mth, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY mth) AS month_index
  FROM month_indices
),

sales_data AS (
  SELECT
    ms.product_id,
    nm.month_index,
    ms.qty AS sales_amount
  FROM monthly_sales ms
  JOIN numbered_months nm ON ms.mth = nm.mth
  WHERE ms.product_id IN (4160, 7790)
    AND nm.month_index BETWEEN 1 AND 36
),

-- Calculate centered moving average (CMA) using 12-month overlapping windows for each product
cma_calc AS (
  SELECT
    s1.product_id,
    s1.month_index,
    (
      (SELECT AVG(sales_amount) FROM sales_data s2
       WHERE s2.product_id = s1.product_id
         AND s2.month_index BETWEEN s1.month_index - 6 AND s1.month_index + 5) +
      (SELECT AVG(sales_amount) FROM sales_data s3
       WHERE s3.product_id = s1.product_id
         AND s3.month_index BETWEEN s1.month_index - 5 AND s1.month_index + 6)
    ) / 2.0 AS cma_value
  FROM sales_data s1
  WHERE s1.month_index BETWEEN 7 AND 30
),

-- Join sales and CMA to get sales-to-CMA ratio
sales_cma_ratio AS (
  SELECT
    sd.product_id,
    sd.month_index,
    sd.sales_amount,
    c.cma_value,
    (CAST(sd.sales_amount AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(c.cma_value, 0)) AS sales_to_cma_ratio
  FROM sales_data sd
  JOIN cma_calc c
    ON sd.product_id = c.product_id
   AND sd.month_index = c.month_index
  WHERE sd.month_index BETWEEN 7 AND 30
),

-- Using weighted regression method to forecast sales for 2018 (months 25 to 36 are 2018 months in the 3-year span)
weights AS (
  SELECT
    month_index,
    CASE WHEN month_index BETWEEN 7 AND 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS weight
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT month_index FROM sales_data)
),

weighted_sums AS (
  SELECT
    sd.product_id,
    SUM(sd.month_index * w.weight) AS sum_xw,
    SUM(sd.sales_amount * w.weight) AS sum_yw,
    SUM(sd.month_index * sd.sales_amount * w.weight) AS sum_xyw,
    SUM(sd.month_index * sd.month_index * w.weight) AS sum_x2w,
    SUM(w.weight) AS sum_w
  FROM sales_data sd
  JOIN weights w ON sd.month_index = w.month_index
  GROUP BY sd.product_id
),

regression_params AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    (sum_w * sum_xyw - sum_xw * sum_yw) * 1.0 / NULLIF((sum_w * sum_x2w - sum_xw * sum_xw), 0) AS slope,
    (sum_yw - (sum_w * sum_xyw - sum_xw * sum_yw) * 1.0 / NULLIF((sum_w * sum_x2w - sum_xw * sum_xw), 0) * sum_xw) * 1.0 / NULLIF(sum_w, 0) AS intercept
  FROM weighted_sums
),

forecast_2018 AS (
  SELECT
    rp.product_id,
    m.month_index,

  JOIN (SELECT 25 AS month_index UNION SELECT 26 UNION SELECT 27 UNION SELECT 28 UNION SELECT 29 UNION SELECT 30 UNION SELECT 31 UNION SELECT 32 UNION SELECT 33 UNION SELECT 34 UNION SELECT 35 UNION SELECT 36) m
),

avg_forecast_annual_sales AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    AVG(forecasted_sales) AS avg_annual_sales
  FROM forecast_2018
  GROUP BY product_id
)

SELECT product_id, avg_annual_sales
FROM avg_forecast_annual_sales
ORDER BY product_id;

# Explanation of Metrics

## 1. Sales-to-CMA Ratio
- **Definition**: This ratio compares actual sales to the centered moving average (CMA) of sales.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Centered Moving Average (CMA)**: The CMA is a smoothed value of sales calculated over a rolling 12-month period. It averages sales from the months before and after a given month, specifically using two overlapping windows (5 months before and 6 months after, and vice versa).
  - **Sales-to-CMA Ratio**: The ratio is computed by dividing the actual sales amount for a month by its corresponding CMA value. A ratio greater than 2 indicates that the actual sales are more than twice the smoothed average for that period, suggesting significantly higher-than-average sales.

## 2. 12-Month Overlapping Windows
- **Definition**: A method to smooth sales data over time by averaging values in a specified window.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Window Size**: The window spans 12 months, with the specific approach involving overlapping periods. 
  - **First Window**: For a given month, this window includes 5 months before and 6 months after.
  - **Second Window**: Another window includes 6 months before and 5 months after the given month.
  - **Averaging**: Sales data is averaged over these two overlapping windows to compute the CMA. This method smooths out fluctuations by considering both the past and future sales in the calculation.

## 3. Restriction to the 7th and 30th Months
- **Definition**: A filter applied to focus calculations within a specific range of months.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Time Range**: Only the months between the 7th and 30th time steps (which correspond to specific periods) are considered for calculating the CMA and ratio.
  - **Purpose**: This restriction is used to avoid edge effects in the data where the moving average might be less reliable (e.g., at the very beginning or end of the available data). By focusing on these months, the calculations are more stable and meaningful.

      WHEN f.departure_airport = a.code THEN a.city
      ELSE b.city

      WHEN f.departure_airport = a.code THEN b.city
      ELSE a.city

    a.longitude AS lon1,
    b.latitude AS lat2,

  FROM flights f

  JOIN airports_data b ON f.arrival_airport = b.code
  WHERE a.city = 'Abakan' OR b.city = 'Abakan'
),

  SELECT
    CASE WHEN city1 < city2 THEN city1 ELSE city2 END AS city1,
    CASE WHEN city1 < city2 THEN city2 ELSE city1 END AS city2,
    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2
  FROM AbakanRoutes
),
Distances AS (

    2 * 6371 * ASIN(
      SQRT(
        POWER(SIN(RADIANS(lat2 - lat1) / 2), 2) +
        COS(RADIANS(lat1)) * COS(RADIANS(lat2)) *
        POWER(SIN(RADIANS(lon2 - lon1) / 2), 2)

# Flight Route Distance Calculation

## Introduction

This document describes the method used to calculate the distance between two cities for flight routes. The calculation is based on the Haversine formula, which is commonly used to find the shortest distance between two points on a sphere given their latitude and longitude. This method is especially useful for determining flight distances between airports located in different cities around the world.

## City and Coordinate Extraction

For each flight, the following data is obtained:

- **Departure city** (referred to as `from_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).
- **Arrival city** (referred to as `to_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).

The coordinates are extracted as decimal values, with longitude and latitude represented in degrees. This ensures that trigonometric operations can be applied during the distance calculation.

## Haversine Formula

The Haversine formula is used to calculate the great-circle distance between two points on a sphere using their latitude and longitude. The formula is given as:

\[
d = 2r \cdot \arcsin\left(\sqrt{\sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) + \cos(\phi_1) \cdot \cos(\phi_2) \cdot \sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \lambda}{2}\right)}\right)
\]

Where:

- \( d \) is the distance between the two points (in kilometers).
- \( r \) is the radius of the Earth (approximately 6371 km).
- \( \phi_1 \) and \( \phi_2 \) are the latitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \phi = \phi_2 - \phi_1 \) is the difference in latitudes.
- \( \lambda_1 \) and \( \lambda_2 \) are the longitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \lambda = \lambda_2 - \lambda_1 \) is the difference in longitudes.

### Conversion to Radians

Since the input coordinates are in degrees, they must be converted to radians before applying the Haversine formula. This conversion is done using the formula:

\[
\text{radians} = \text{degrees} \times \frac{\pi}{180}
\]

## Symmetry of Routes

To identify unique flight routes between two cities, we standardize the order of cities in each route. Specifically, we ensure that the lexicographically smaller city name is always listed as the first city (`city1`), and the larger city is listed as the second city (`city2`). This ensures that a flight from City A to City B is treated the same as a flight from City B to City A.

## Average Route Distance

Once the distances for all flights between two cities are computed, the average distance for each city pair is calculated by summing the distances and dividing by the total number of flights between those cities:

\[
\text{Average Distance} = \frac{\sum \text{Flight Distances}}{\text{Number of Flights}}
\]

## Conclusion

This method of flight route distance calculation provides a reliable way to determine the great-circle distance between cities based on the coordinates of their respective airports. The use of the Haversine formula ensures accurate results for distances on the Earth's surface, making it ideal for aviation and travel analysis.

        MIN(c.DurationMin) AS MinDuration,

        SUM(COALESCE(i.Revenue,0)) AS TotalRevenue
    FROM Categories c
    LEFT JOIN InvoiceData i ON c.TrackId = i.TrackId
    GROUP BY c.DurationCategory
)

WITH sales_us AS (
  SELECT 
    s.prod_id,
    c.cust_city AS city,
    t.calendar_quarter_id,
    s.promo_id,
    s.amount_sold
  FROM sales s
  JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_iso_code = 'US'
    AND s.promo_id = 999
    AND t.calendar_quarter_id IN (1772, 1776)
),

city_sales AS (
  SELECT city, calendar_quarter_id, SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales
  FROM sales_us
  GROUP BY city, calendar_quarter_id
),

city_growth AS (
  SELECT 
    city,
    MAX(CASE WHEN calendar_quarter_id = 1772 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_2019_q4,
    MAX(CASE WHEN calendar_quarter_id = 1776 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_2020_q4
  FROM city_sales
  GROUP BY city
  HAVING sales_2020_q4 >= 1.2 * sales_2019_q4
),

prod_city_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    su.prod_id,
    su.city,
    su.calendar_quarter_id,
    SUM(su.amount_sold) AS total_sales
  FROM sales_us su
  WHERE su.city IN (SELECT city FROM city_growth)
  GROUP BY su.prod_id, su.city, su.calendar_quarter_id
),

prod_qtr_sales AS (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    calendar_quarter_id,
    SUM(total_sales) AS total_sales
  FROM prod_city_sales
  GROUP BY prod_id, calendar_quarter_id
),

all_prods_per_qtr AS (
  SELECT

    COUNT(DISTINCT prod_id) AS prod_count
  FROM prod_qtr_sales
  GROUP BY calendar_quarter_id
),

prod_sales_ranked AS (

),

total_sales_per_qtr AS (

prod_share AS (

),

FROM prod_share_change
ORDER BY share_change ASC

The query to count overtakes in the first five laps by category is too complex for execution in the current environment size, leading to interruption. I will simplify the approach by counting overtakes by category directly from lap_positions for the first 5 laps, joined with retirements, pit stops, and grid positions for classification.

```sql
WITH first_five_laps AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, lap
  FROM lap_times
  WHERE lap <= 5
),
retired_drivers AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap AS retirement_lap
  FROM retirements
),
pit_events AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap
  FROM pit_stops
),
start_grid_positions AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, grid
  FROM results
  WHERE grid > 0
),
overtakes AS (
  SELECT 
    curr.race_id,
    curr.lap,
    prev.driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
    curr.driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
    curr.position AS overtaking_position,
    prev.position AS overtaken_position
  FROM lap_positions curr
  JOIN lap_positions prev ON curr.race_id = prev.race_id
    AND curr.lap = prev.lap + 1
    AND curr.position = prev.position - 1
    AND curr.driver_id != prev.driver_id
    AND curr.race_id IN (SELECT race_id FROM first_five_laps)
),
overtake_labels AS (
  SELECT
    o.*,
    CASE
      WHEN r.retirement_lap = o.lap THEN 'R'
      WHEN p_current.lap = o.lap OR p_prev.lap = o.lap - 1 THEN 'P'
      WHEN o.lap = 1 
           AND s1.grid IS NOT NULL AND s2.grid IS NOT NULL
           AND ABS(s1.grid - s2.grid) <= 2 THEN 'S'
      ELSE 'T'
    END AS category
  FROM overtakes o
  LEFT JOIN retired_drivers r ON o.race_id = r.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = r.driver_id 
  LEFT JOIN pit_events p_current ON o.race_id = p_current.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = p_current.driver_id AND o.lap = p_current.lap
  LEFT JOIN pit_events p_prev ON o.race_id = p_prev.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = p_prev.driver_id AND o.lap - 1 = p_prev.lap
  LEFT JOIN start_grid_positions s1 ON o.race_id = s1.race_id AND o.overtaking_driver_id = s1.driver_id
  LEFT JOIN start_grid_positions s2 ON o.race_id = s2.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = s2.driver_id
)
SELECT category AS overtake_category, COUNT(*) AS overtakes_count
FROM overtake_labels
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY CASE category
  WHEN 'R' THEN 1
  WHEN 'P' THEN 2
  WHEN 'S' THEN 3
  WHEN 'T' THEN 4
  ELSE 5
END;
```

In the first five laps of the race, how many overtakes occurred in each category—retirements, pit stops, start-related overtakes, and standard on-track passes?

Provided benchmark documentation:
# Overtake Label Classification

In racing, overtakes are categorized into different states based on specific conditions, reflecting the circumstances in which the overtaking occurred. Below are the classifications and their detailed explanations:

## 1. R (Retirement) - Overtake during Retirement
An overtake is labeled as **R (Retirement)** if the overtaken driver retired on the same lap as the overtake. This indicates that the overtake occurred just before or during the overtaken driver's retirement, meaning they could no longer continue the race after that lap.

## 2. P (Pit) - Overtake related to Pit Stops
An overtake is classified as **P (Pit)** under two scenarios:
   - **Pit Entry**: If the overtake occurred while the overtaken driver was entering the pit lane, and the driver pitted on the same lap, it indicates that the overtaking happened due to the overtaken driver reducing speed to enter the pit lane.
   - **Pit Exit**: If the overtake occurred as the overtaken driver was exiting the pit lane, especially if the driver pitted on the previous lap and the time gap between the drivers was less than a typical pit stop duration. This suggests that the overtake happened while the overtaken driver was potentially at a lower speed, rejoining the race track from the pit lane.

## 3. S (Start) - Overtake at Race Start
If the overtake took place on the first lap of the race, and the two drivers were within two grid positions of each other at the start, the overtake is classified as **S (Start)**. This classification indicates that the overtake was part of the initial racing shuffle during the race's launch phase, where close position changes are common.

## 4. T (Track) - Overtake under Normal Racing Conditions
If none of the above conditions apply, the overtake is categorized as **T (Track)**, meaning it occurred during normal racing conditions on the track, without any external factors like pit stops or retirements influencing the outcome. This is the default classification for overtakes that happen during regular competition.

---

These classifications help to identify and record the context of each overtake with clarity, ensuring accurate representation of race dynamics.

WITH first_five_laps AS (
  SELECT race_id, lap
  FROM lap_times
  WHERE lap <= 5
  GROUP BY race_id, lap
),
pit_events AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap, MIN(time_in_pit) AS pit_in_lap
  FROM (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap,
           CASE WHEN pit_in_time IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE NULL END AS time_in_pit
    FROM pit_stops
  )
  GROUP BY race_id, driver_id, lap
),
retired_drivers AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap AS retirement_lap
  FROM retirements
),
start_grid_positions AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, grid
  FROM results
  WHERE grid > 0
),
overtakes AS (
  /*
    We define overtakes by position changes between laps (lap_times), considering lap, driver, and position.
    The overtaken driver is the one who loses position from one lap to the next.
  */
  SELECT 
    curr.race_id,
    curr.lap,
    prev.driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
    curr.driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
    curr.position AS overtaking_position,
    prev.position AS overtaken_position
  FROM lap_positions curr
  JOIN lap_positions prev ON curr.race_id = prev.race_id 
    AND curr.driver_id != prev.driver_id  /* Different drivers */
    AND curr.lap = prev.lap + 1
    AND curr.position = prev.position - 1
    AND curr.race_id IN (SELECT race_id FROM first_five_laps)
),
overlap_labels AS (
  SELECT
    o.race_id,
    o.lap,
    o.overtaking_driver_id,
    o.overtaken_driver_id,
    CASE
      WHEN r.retirement_lap = o.lap THEN 'R'
      WHEN p1.lap = o.lap THEN 'P'
      WHEN p2.lap = o.lap - 1 THEN 'P'
      WHEN o.lap = 1

I will simplify the approach by counting overtakes by category directly from lap_positions for the first 5 laps, joined with retirements, pit stops, and grid positions for classification.

```sql
WITH first_five_laps AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, lap
  FROM lap_times
  WHERE lap <= 5
),
retired_drivers AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap AS retirement_lap
  FROM retirements
),
pit_events AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap
  FROM pit_stops
),
start_grid_positions AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, grid
  FROM results
  WHERE grid > 0
),
overtakes AS (
  SELECT 
    curr.race_id,
    curr.lap,
    prev.driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
    curr.driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
    curr.position AS overtaking_position,
    prev.position AS overtaken_position
  FROM lap_positions curr
  JOIN lap_positions prev ON curr.race_id = prev.race_id
    AND curr.lap = prev.lap + 1
    AND curr.position = prev.position - 1
    AND curr.driver_id != prev.driver_id
    AND curr.race_id IN (SELECT race_id FROM first_five_laps)
),
overtake_labels AS (
  SELECT
    o.*,
    CASE
      WHEN r.retirement_lap = o.lap THEN 'R'
      WHEN p_current.lap = o.lap OR p_prev.lap = o.lap - 1 THEN 'P'
      WHEN o.lap = 1 
           AND s1.grid IS NOT NULL AND s2.grid IS NOT NULL
           AND ABS(s1.grid - s2.grid) <= 2 THEN 'S'
      ELSE 'T'
    END AS category
  FROM overtakes o
  LEFT JOIN retired_drivers r ON o.race_id = r.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = r.driver_id 
  LEFT JOIN pit_events p_current ON o.race_id = p_current.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = p_current.driver_id AND o.lap = p_current.lap
  LEFT JOIN pit_events p_prev ON o.race_id = p_prev.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = p_prev.driver_id AND o.lap - 1 = p_prev.lap
  LEFT JOIN start_grid_positions s1 ON o.race_id = s1.race_id AND o.overtaking_driver_id = s1.driver_id
  LEFT JOIN start_grid_positions s2 ON o.race_id = s2.race_id AND o.overtaken_driver_id = s2.driver_id
)
SELECT category AS overtake_category, COUNT(*) AS overtakes_count
FROM overtake_labels
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY CASE category
  WHEN 'R' THEN 1
  WHEN 'P' THEN 2
  WHEN 'S' THEN 3
  WHEN 'T' THEN 4

Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.

WITH month_interest AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y-%m', date) AS month,
    interest,
    composition/index AS avg_composition
  FROM interest_metrics
  WHERE date >= '2018-09-01' AND date < '2019-09-01'
),
max_interest_per_month AS (
  SELECT 
    month,
    interest AS max_interest,
    AVG(avg_composition) AS max_index_composition
  FROM month_interest
  GROUP BY month
  HAVING max_index_composition = MAX(AVG(avg_composition)) OVER (PARTITION BY month)
),
rolling AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    max_interest,
    max_index_composition,
    AVG(max_index_composition) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_avg
  FROM max_interest_per_month
),
previous_months AS (
  SELECT
    r1.month,
    r1.max_interest,
    r1.max_index_composition,
    r1.rolling_avg,
    r2.max_interest AS prev1_max_interest,
    r2.max_index_composition AS prev1_max_index_composition,
    r3.max_interest AS prev2_max_interest,
    r3.max_index_composition AS prev2_max_index_composition
  FROM rolling r1
  LEFT JOIN rolling r2 ON date(r2.month || '-01') = date(r1.month || '-01', '-1 month')
  LEFT JOIN rolling r3 ON date(r3.month || '-01') = date(r1.month || '-01', '-2 month')
)
SELECT * FROM previous_months

The packaging_relations table has columns that indicate a packaging item contains other packaging items, with packaging_id as the parent and contains_id as the child, along with a quantity (qty) for the number of child items in the parent packaging.

The packaging table contains packaging items with id and name.

I will write a recursive query to expand all nested packaging_relations from a parent packaging to its leaf level items, and calculate the total quantity of leaf items per final packaging. Then I will average these total quantities across all final packaging.

The quantity multiplication needs to be considered when recursively expanding packaging combinations.

Here is the SQL query that calculates the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations considering the quantities of nested packaging items:

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE
ExpandedPackaging AS (
  SELECT
    packaging_id AS final_packaging_id,
    contains_id AS child_packaging_id,
    qty AS child_qty
  FROM packaging_relations
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    ep.final_packaging_id,
    pr.contains_id,
    ep.child_qty * pr.qty
  FROM packaging_relations pr
  JOIN ExpandedPackaging ep ON pr.packaging_id = ep.child_packaging_id
),
LeafPackaging AS (
  SELECT
    ep.final_packaging_id,
    ep.child_packaging_id,
    ep.child_qty
  FROM ExpandedPackaging ep
  LEFT JOIN packaging_relations pr ON ep.child_packaging_id = pr.packaging_id
  WHERE pr.packaging_id IS NULL
),
AggregatedQuantities AS (
  SELECT
    final_packaging_id,
    SUM(child_qty) AS total_quantity
  FROM LeafPackaging
  GROUP BY final_packaging_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_quantity) AS average_total_quantity
FROM AggregatedQuantities;
```

WITH Team_Wins AS (
  SELECT
    L.id AS league_id,
    T.team_api_id,
    T.team_long_name,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN M.home_team_api_id = T.team_api_id AND M.home_team_goal > M.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) +
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN M.away_team_api_id = T.team_api_id AND M.away_team_goal > M.home_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_wins
  FROM Team T
  CROSS JOIN League L
  LEFT JOIN Match M ON (M.league_id = L.id AND (M.home_team_api_id = T.team_api_id OR M.away_team_api_id = T.team_api_id))
  GROUP BY L.id, T.team_api_id
),
League_Min_Wins AS (
  SELECT league_id, MIN(total_wins) AS min_wins
  FROM Team_Wins
  GROUP BY league_id
),
League_Fewest_Wins AS (
  SELECT tw.league_id, tw.team_api_id, tw.team_long_name, tw.total_wins
  FROM Team_Wins tw
  JOIN League_Min_Wins lmw ON tw.league_id = lmw.league_id AND tw.total_wins = lmw.min_wins
  GROUP BY tw.league_id
)
SELECT league_id, team_api_id, team_long_name, total_wins
FROM League_Fewest_Wins;

WITH first_targets AS (
    SELECT 
        session_id,
        MIN(event_index) AS first_target_index
    FROM (
        SELECT
            session_id,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY event_time) AS event_index,
            path
        FROM activity_log
        WHERE path IN ('/detail', '/complete')
    )
    GROUP BY session_id
), pre_target_events AS (
    SELECT 
        a.session_id,
        a.path,
        a.search_type,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.session_id ORDER BY a.event_time) AS event_index
    FROM activity_log a
    JOIN first_targets f ON a.session_id = f.session_id
    WHERE a.search_type != '' AND
          a.event_time < (SELECT MIN(event_time) FROM activity_log al2 
                          WHERE al2.session_id = a.session_id AND al2.path IN ('/detail', '/complete'))
), pre_count_per_session AS (
    SELECT 
        session_id,
        COUNT(*) AS pre_event_count
    FROM pre_target_events
    GROUP BY session_id
), min_pre_count AS (
    SELECT MIN(pre_event_count) AS min_count FROM pre_count_per_session
), min_sessions AS (
    SELECT session_id FROM pre_count_per_session WHERE pre_event_count = (SELECT min_count FROM min_pre_count)
)
SELECT p.session_id, p.path, p.search_type
FROM pre_target_events p
JOIN min_sessions m ON p.session_id = m.session_id
ORDER BY p.session_id, p.event_index;

WITH customer_sales AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        MIN(rental_date) AS first_purchase,
        SUM(amount) AS lifetime_sales
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
), sales_within_periods AS (
    SELECT
        p.customer_id,
        cs.lifetime_sales,
        SUM(CASE WHEN p.rental_date <= cs.first_purchase + INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS sales_7_days,
        SUM(CASE WHEN p.rental_date <= cs.first_purchase + INTERVAL 30 DAY THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS sales_30_days
    FROM payment p
    JOIN customer_sales cs ON p.customer_id = cs.customer_id
    GROUP BY p.customer_id, cs.lifetime_sales
)
SELECT
    AVG(lifetime_sales) AS avg_lifetime_sales,
    AVG(sales_7_days * 100.0 / lifetime_sales) AS avg_7_day_pct,
    AVG(sales_30_days * 100.0 / lifetime_sales) AS avg_30_day_pct
FROM sales_within_periods
WHERE lifetime_sales > 0;
```

WITH English_Students AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    st.StudentID,
    st.StudLastName,
    ss.Grade
  FROM Students st
  JOIN Student_Schedules ss ON st.StudentID = ss.StudentID
  JOIN Classes c ON ss.ClassID = c.ClassID

  WHERE sub.SubjectName LIKE '%English%'
    AND ss.ClassStatus = 2
),
Ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    es.StudentID,
    es.StudLastName,
    es.Grade,

  FROM English_Students es
),
TotalCount AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total FROM English_Students
),
Quintiles AS (
  SELECT 
    r.StudLastName,
    r.Grade,
    r.Rank,
    t.Total,
    CASE 
      WHEN (r.Rank * 1.0 / t.Total) <= 0.2 THEN 'First'
      WHEN (r.Rank * 1.0 / t.Total) <= 0.4 THEN 'Second'
      WHEN (r.Rank * 1.0 / t.Total) <= 0.6 THEN 'Third'
      WHEN (r.Rank * 1.0 / t.Total) <= 0.8 THEN 'Fourth'
      ELSE 'Fifth'
    END AS Quintile
  FROM Ranked r
  CROSS JOIN TotalCount t
)
SELECT StudLastName AS LastName, Quintile
FROM Quintiles
ORDER BY CASE Quintile
  WHEN 'First' THEN 1
  WHEN 'Second' THEN 2
  WHEN 'Third' THEN 3

Provided benchmark documentation:
## Projection Calculation Method

### Steps for Projection Calculation

1. **Aggregate Historical Sales Data**

   - **Data Collection**: Gather sales data for products sold in France, including sales amounts each month for the years 2019, 2020, and 2021.
   - **Summarize Sales**: Sum up the sales amounts for each product, country, month, and year.

2. **Calculate Average Sales**

   - **Monthly Averages**: Compute the average sales amount for each product and month across all available months to establish a baseline of typical sales.

3. **Project Sales for 2021**

   - **Identify Changes**: Determine how sales changed from 2019 to 2020 for each product and month. Calculate the percentage change in sales from 2019 to 2020.
   - **Apply Changes**: Use this percentage change to estimate the sales for each month in 2021.

   **Projection Formula**:
   - For 2021:
     - Calculate the difference in sales between 2020 and 2019.
     - Compute the percentage change relative to 2019 sales.
     - Apply this percentage change to the 2020 sales to estimate 2021 sales.
     - The formula used in the SQL query is:

       ```plaintext
       (((Sales in 2020 - Sales in 2019) / Sales in 2019) * Sales in 2020) + Sales in 2020
       ```

     - This formula calculates the projected sales for 2021 based on the observed trend from 2019 to 2020.

   - For other years (not 2021):
     - Use the average sales value calculated for each month.

4. **Adjust for Currency Conversion**

   - **Conversion Rates**: Convert the projected sales figures into USD using monthly conversion rates.
   - **Currency Adjustment**: Multiply the projected sales figures by the conversion rates to adjust to USD. If specific rates are not available, use a default rate of 1.

5. **Calculate Monthly Averages in USD**

   - **Monthly Projections**: Compute the average projected sales for each month in 2021, adjusting for currency conversion. Round the results to two decimal places.

6. **Compile Results**

   - **Organize Data**: Arrange the projected sales figures in a report, showing the estimated sales for each month in USD.

### Summary

The projection calculation involves analyzing historical sales data from 2019 and 2020 to determine trends, applying these trends to estimate sales for 2021, and adjusting for currency differences. The result is a forecast of monthly sales in USD for 2021.

WITH sales_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_id,
    s.year,
    s.month,
    s.sales_amount,
    c.currency_code
  FROM sales s
  JOIN countries co ON s.country_id = co.country_id
  JOIN currency c ON co.currency_id = c.currency_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'France'
    AND s.promo_total_id = 1
    AND s.channel_total_id = 1
    AND s.year IN (2019, 2020)
),
-- Aggregate sales by product, year, month
sales_agg AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    year,
    month,
    SUM(sales_amount) AS total_sales,
    MAX(currency_code) AS currency_code
  FROM sales_filtered
  GROUP BY product_id, year, month
),
-- Calculate growth rate from 2019 to 2020
growth_calc AS (
  SELECT
    a.product_id,
    a.month,
    CASE WHEN base_sales = 0 THEN 0 ELSE ((next_sales - base_sales) * 1.0 / base_sales) END AS growth_rate,
    base_sales,
    next_sales
  FROM (
    SELECT
      product_id,
      month,
      SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS base_sales,
      SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2020 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS next_sales
    FROM sales_agg
    GROUP BY product_id, month
  ) a
),
-- Project sales for 2021 using the given formula
sales_2021_proj AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    month,
    (((next_sales - base_sales) * 1.0 / NULLIF(base_sales, 0)) * next_sales) + next_sales AS projected_sales,
    MAX(currency_code) AS currency_code
  FROM (
    SELECT
      g.product_id,
      g.month,
      g.growth_rate,
      b.base_sales,
      b.next_sales,
      a.currency_code
    FROM growth_calc g
    JOIN (
      SELECT product_id, month, base_sales, next_sales
      FROM (
        SELECT product_id, month, 
               SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS base_sales,
               SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2020 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS next_sales
        FROM sales_agg
        GROUP BY product_id, month
      ) t
    ) b ON g.product_id = b.product_id AND g.month = b.month
    JOIN sales_agg a ON a.product_id = g.product_id AND a.year = 2020 AND a.month = g.month
  ) sub
  GROUP BY product_id, month
),
-- Get monthly average projected sales in local currency
monthly_avg_sales AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    AVG(projected_sales) AS avg_sales_local,
    MAX(currency_code) AS currency_code
  FROM sales_2021_proj
  GROUP BY month
),
-- Get currency exchange rates for France currency to USD for 2021
currency_rates_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    t.month,
    co.currency_code,
    COALESCE(cu.exchange_rate_to_usd, 1) AS exchange_rate
  FROM times t
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT currency_code FROM monthly_avg_sales
  ) co
  LEFT JOIN currency cu ON cu.currency_code = co.currency_code
  WHERE t.year = 2021
),
-- Convert projected sales to USD
monthly_avg_usd AS (
  SELECT
    m.month,
    ROUND(m.avg_sales_local * cr.exchange_rate, 2) AS avg_sales_usd
  FROM monthly_avg_sales m
  JOIN currency_rates_2021 cr ON m.currency_code = cr.currency_code AND m.month = cr.month
),
-- Find the median of the average monthly projected sales in USD for 2021
median_calc AS (
  SELECT avg_sales_usd
  FROM monthly_avg_usd
  ORDER BY avg_sales_usd
  LIMIT 1
  OFFSET (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM monthly_avg_usd) / 2
)
SELECT avg_sales_usd AS median_avg_monthly_projected_sales_usd
FROM median_calc;

  CROSS JOIN france_country fc
  WHERE s.promo_id = 1
    AND s.channel_id = 1
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
  GROUP BY s.prod_id, t.calendar_year, t.calendar_month_number
),
growth_calc AS (
  SELECT
    fs2019.prod_id,
    fs2019.month,
    fs2019.total_amount_sold AS sales_2019,
    IFNULL(fs2020.total_amount_sold, 0) AS sales_2020,
    CASE WHEN fs2019.total_amount_sold = 0 THEN 0
         ELSE ((fs2020.total_amount_sold - fs2019.total_amount_sold) * 1.0 / fs2019.total_amount_sold) END AS growth_rate
  FROM filtered_sales fs2019
  LEFT JOIN filtered_sales fs2020 ON fs2019.prod_id = fs2020.prod_id AND fs2019.month = fs2020.month AND fs2020.year = 2020
  WHERE fs2019.year = 2019
),
projected_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    gc.prod_id,
    gc.month,
    ((gc.growth_rate * gc.sales_2020) + gc.sales_2020) AS projected_sales
  FROM growth_calc gc
),
monthly_avg_sales AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    AVG(projected_sales) AS avg_sales
  FROM projected_2021
  GROUP BY month
),
currency_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    c.month,
    c.to_us AS exchange_rate
  FROM currency c
  WHERE c.year = 2021
    AND c.country = 'France'
),
monthly_avg_usd AS (
  SELECT
    m.month,
    ROUND(m.avg_sales * COALESCE(c.exchange_rate, 1), 2) AS avg_sales_usd
  FROM monthly_avg_sales m
  LEFT JOIN currency_2021 c ON m.month = c.month
),
median_value AS (
  SELECT avg_sales_usd
  FROM monthly_avg_usd
  ORDER BY avg_sales_usd
  LIMIT 1 OFFSET (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM monthly_avg_usd) / 2
)
SELECT avg_sales_usd AS median_avg_monthly_projected_sales_usd
FROM median_value;
```

I noticed that batsman_scored does not directly link with player_id. So we cannot join player_match to batsman_scored on player_id. Instead, I will join them using match_id, over_id, and ball_id because they uniquely identify an event in the match, and player_match provides player_id and team_id for the match. Also, team names are stored under team.name, and match winner and participants are linked by team_id in the match table. I will write a query that:
- Identifies the losing team for each match,
- Sums runs scored by each player in that match (joined on match_id and ball-by-ball event),
- Filters players who scored at least 100 runs while playing for the losing team,
- Retrieves their names.

Here is the final SQL.
```sql
WITH losing_teams AS (
  SELECT match_id, 
         CASE 
           WHEN match_winner = team_1 THEN team_2
           ELSE team_1
         END AS losing_team_id
  FROM match
), player_runs AS (
  SELECT pm.match_id, pm.player_id, pm.team_id, SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS total_runs
  FROM player_match pm
  JOIN batsman_scored bs 
    ON pm.match_id = bs.match_id
  -- Join ball_by_ball to get player_id who played each ball (batsman)
  JOIN ball_by_ball bb 
    ON bs.match_id = bb.match_id 
   AND bs.over_id = bb.over_id 
   AND bs.ball_id = bb.ball_id
  WHERE bb.batsman = pm.player_id
  GROUP BY pm.match_id, pm.player_id, pm.team_id
), losing_top_scorers AS (
  SELECT pr.player_id
  FROM player_runs pr
  JOIN losing_teams lt 
    ON pr.match_id = lt.match_id 
   AND pr.team_id = lt.losing_team_id
  WHERE pr.total_runs >= 100
)
SELECT DISTINCT p.player_name
FROM losing_top_scorers lts
JOIN player p ON lts.player_id = p.player_id;
```

WITH DirectorMovies AS (
  SELECT
    dm.name_id AS director_id,
    n.name AS director_name,
    m.id AS movie_id,
    m.duration AS runtime,
    r.avg_rating AS rating,
    r.total_votes AS num_votes,
    m.year AS start_year
  FROM director_mapping dm
  JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
  JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
  LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
),

Aggregations AS (
  SELECT
    director_id,
    director_name,
    COUNT(movie_id) AS movie_count,
    ROUND(AVG(runtime)) AS avg_runtime,
    ROUND(AVG(rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
    SUM(num_votes) AS total_votes,
    MIN(rating) AS min_rating,
    MAX(rating) AS max_rating,
    SUM(runtime) AS total_runtime,
    MIN(start_year) AS min_year,
    MAX(start_year) AS max_year
  FROM DirectorMovies
  GROUP BY director_id, director_name
),

InterMovieDuration AS (
  SELECT
    director_id,
    CASE
      WHEN movie_count = 1 THEN 0
      ELSE ROUND(CAST(max_year - min_year AS FLOAT) / (movie_count - 1))
    END AS avg_inter_movie_duration
  FROM Aggregations
)

SELECT
  a.director_id,
  a.director_name,
  a.movie_count,
  COALESCE(imd.avg_inter_movie_duration, 0) AS avg_inter_movie_duration,
  COALESCE(a.avg_rating, 0) AS avg_rating,
  COALESCE(a.total_votes, 0) AS total_votes,
  COALESCE(a.min_rating, 0) AS min_rating,
  COALESCE(a.max_rating, 0) AS max_rating,
  COALESCE(a.total_runtime, 0) AS total_movie_duration
FROM Aggregations a
LEFT JOIN InterMovieDuration imd ON a.director_id = imd.director_id

The correct column names are snake_case style (e.g., driver_id, race_id). Also, pit_stops table has lap column to exclude pit laps, and retirements table can be used to exclude retired drivers.

I will write the SQL with these correct column names and using the correct logic:
- Use lap_positions to count overtakes:
  * driver A overtakes driver B if A's position improves relative to B's between consecutive laps, excluding lap 1
- Exclude laps where pit stop happens (lap or lap-1 in pit_stops for that driver in that race)
- Exclude drivers who retired (from retirements)
- Get drivers who were overtaken more times than they overtook others

I proceed with one SQL query to find those drivers by their full_name.
```sql
WITH lap_changes AS (
    SELECT 
        curr.race_id,
        curr.lap,
        curr.driver_id,
        curr.position AS curr_position,
        prev.position AS prev_position
    FROM lap_positions curr
    JOIN lap_positions prev ON curr.race_id = prev.race_id AND curr.driver_id = prev.driver_id AND curr.lap = prev.lap + 1
    WHERE curr.lap > 1
),
overtaking_events AS (
    SELECT
        lc1.race_id,
        lc1.lap,
        lc1.driver_id AS overtaker,
        lc2.driver_id AS overtaken
    FROM lap_changes lc1
    JOIN lap_changes lc2 ON lc1.race_id = lc2.race_id AND lc1.lap = lc2.lap
    WHERE lc1.curr_position < lc2.curr_position AND lc1.prev_position > lc2.prev_position
),
filtered_overtaking_events AS (
    SELECT oe.*
    FROM overtaking_events oe
    LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps1 ON oe.race_id = ps1.race_id AND oe.overtaker = ps1.driver_id AND (ps1.lap = oe.lap OR ps1.lap = oe.lap - 1)
    LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps2 ON oe.race_id = ps2.race_id AND oe.overtaken = ps2.driver_id AND (ps2.lap = oe.lap OR ps2.lap = oe.lap - 1)
    LEFT JOIN retirements r1 ON oe.race_id = r1.race_id AND oe.overtaker = r1.driver_id
    LEFT JOIN retirements r2 ON oe.race_id = r2.race_id AND oe.overtaken = r2.driver_id
    WHERE ps1.race_id IS NULL AND ps2.race_id IS NULL AND r1.race_id IS NULL AND r2.race_id IS NULL
),
overtakes_count AS (
    SELECT overtaker AS driver_id, COUNT(*) AS overtakes
    FROM filtered_overtaking_events
    GROUP BY overtaker
),
overtaken_count AS (
    SELECT overtaken AS driver_id, COUNT(*) AS overtaken
    FROM filtered_overtaking_events
    GROUP BY overtaken
)
SELECT 
    d.full_name
FROM drivers d
LEFT JOIN overtakes_count o ON d.driver_id = o.driver_id
LEFT JOIN overtaken_count ot ON d.driver_id = ot.driver_id
WHERE COALESCE(ot.overtaken, 0) > COALESCE(o.overtakes, 0)
ORDER BY d.full_name;
```

LEFT JOIN overtakes_count o ON d.driver_id = o.driver_id
LEFT JOIN overtaken_count ot ON d.driver_id = ot.driver_id

ORDER BY d.full_name;

WITH CustomerOrderTotals AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity) AS TotalSpent
    FROM
        orders o
        JOIN order_details od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID

CustomerGroups AS (
    SELECT
        c.CustomerID,
        cct.CustomerGroup,
        cot.TotalSpent
    FROM
        CustomerOrderTotals cot
        JOIN customergroupthreshold cct ON cot.TotalSpent >= cct.Amount
    WHERE
        cct.Amount = (
            SELECT MAX(Amount)
            FROM customergroupthreshold
            WHERE Amount <= cot.TotalSpent
        )
),
GroupCounts AS (
    SELECT
        CustomerGroup,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS CustomerCount
    FROM
        CustomerGroups
    GROUP BY
        CustomerGroup
),
TotalCustomers AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS TotalCustomerCount
    FROM CustomerOrderTotals
)
SELECT
    gc.CustomerGroup,
    gc.CustomerCount,
    ROUND(100.0 * gc.CustomerCount / tc.TotalCustomerCount, 2) AS PercentageOfTotal
FROM
    GroupCounts gc,
    TotalCustomers tc
ORDER BY
    gc.CustomerGroup;
```

WITH filtered_sales AS (

        sales.prod_id,
        countries.country_id,
        times.calendar_year AS year,
        times.calendar_month_number AS month,
        sales.amount_sold,
        promotions.promo_total_id,
        channels.channel_total_id
    FROM sales
    JOIN countries ON sales.cust_id = countries.country_id
    JOIN promotions ON sales.promo_id = promotions.promo_id
    JOIN channels ON sales.channel_id = channels.channel_id
    JOIN times ON sales.time_id = times.time_id
    WHERE countries.country_name = 'France'
      AND promotions.promo_total_id = 1
      AND channels.channel_total_id = 1
      AND times.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
),
sales_agg AS (
    SELECT
        prod_id,
        year,
        month,
        SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY prod_id, year, month
),
sales_2019 AS (
    SELECT prod_id, month, total_sales AS sales_2019
    FROM sales_agg
    WHERE year = 2019
),
sales_2020 AS (
    SELECT prod_id, month, total_sales AS sales_2020
    FROM sales_agg
    WHERE year = 2020
),
projected_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        s20.prod_id,
        s20.month,
        s20.sales_2020,
        COALESCE(s19.sales_2019, 0) AS sales_2019,
        CASE 
            WHEN s19.sales_2019 = 0 THEN s20.sales_2020
            ELSE (((s20.sales_2020 - s19.sales_2019) * s20.sales_2020) / s19.sales_2019) + s20.sales_2020
        END AS projected_sales
    FROM sales_2020 s20
    LEFT JOIN sales_2019 s19 ON s20.prod_id = s19.prod_id AND s20.month = s19.month
),
currency_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        country AS country_name,
        year,
        month,
        to_us AS exchange_rate_to_usd
    FROM currency
    WHERE country = 'France' AND year = 2021
),
sales_2021_converted AS (
    SELECT
        p.month,
        p.projected_sales,
        c.exchange_rate_to_usd,
        (p.projected_sales * COALESCE(c.exchange_rate_to_usd, 1)) AS projected_sales_usd
    FROM projected_2021 p
    LEFT JOIN currency_2021 c ON p.month = c.month
)
SELECT
    month,
    ROUND(AVG(projected_sales_usd), 2) AS avg_projected_sales_usd
FROM sales_2021_converted
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

What is the average projected monthly sales in USD for France in 2021, considering only product sales with promotions where promo_total_id = 1 and channels where channel_total_id = 1, by taking each product’s monthly sales from 2019 and 2020, calculating the growth rate from 2019 to 2020 for that same product and month, applying this growth rate to project 2021 monthly sales, converting all projected 2021 amounts to USD with the 2021 exchange rates, and finally averaging and listing them by month?

Provided benchmark documentation:
## Projection Calculation Method

### Steps for Projection Calculation

1. **Aggregate Historical Sales Data**

   - **Data Collection**: Gather sales data for products sold in France, including sales amounts each month for the years 2019, 2020, and 2021.
   - **Summarize Sales**: Sum up the sales amounts for each product, country, month, and year.

2. **Calculate Average Sales**

   - **Monthly Averages**: Compute the average sales amount for each product and month across all available months to establish a baseline of typical sales.

3. **Project Sales for 2021**

   - **Identify Changes**: Determine how sales changed from 2019 to 2020 for each product and month. Calculate the percentage change in sales from 2019 to 2020.
   - **Apply Changes**: Use this percentage change to estimate the sales for each month in 2021.

   **Projection Formula**:
   - For 2021:
     - Calculate the difference in sales between 2020 and 2019.
     - Compute the percentage change relative to 2019 sales.
     - Apply this percentage change to the 2020 sales to estimate 2021 sales.
     - The formula used in the SQL query is:

       ```plaintext
       (((Sales in 2020 - Sales in 2019) / Sales in 2019) * Sales in 2020) + Sales in 2020
       ```

     - This formula calculates the projected sales for 2021 based on the observed trend from 2019 to 2020.

   - For other years (not 2021):
     - Use the average sales value calculated for each month.

4. **Adjust for Currency Conversion**

   - **Conversion Rates**: Convert the projected sales figures into USD using monthly conversion rates.
   - **Currency Adjustment**: Multiply the projected sales figures by the conversion rates to adjust to USD. If specific rates are not available, use a default rate of 1.

5. **Calculate Monthly Averages in USD**

   - **Monthly Projections**: Compute the average projected sales for each month in 2021, adjusting for currency conversion. Round the results to two decimal places.

6. **Compile Results**

   - **Organize Data**: Arrange the projected sales figures in a report, showing the estimated sales for each month in USD.

### Summary

The projection calculation involves analyzing historical sales data from 2019 and 2020 to determine trends, applying these trends to estimate sales for 2021, and adjusting for currency differences. The result is a forecast of monthly sales in USD for 2021.

Using them, I will write the SQL that projects the average monthly sales in USD for France in 2021 by applying the growth rate from 2019 to 2020 on product monthly sales, filtering by promo_total_id = 1 and channel_total_id = 1, and converting with 2021 exchange rate.

arguments.sql:
WITH filtered_sales AS (
    SELECT
        sales.prod_id,
        countries.country_id,
        times.calendar_year AS year,
        times.calendar_month_number AS month,
        sales.amount_sold,
        promotions.promo_total_id,
        channels.channel_total_id
    FROM sales
    JOIN countries ON sales.cust_id = countries.country_id
    JOIN promotions ON sales.promo_id = promotions.promo_id
    JOIN channels ON sales.channel_id = channels.channel_id
    JOIN times ON sales.time_id = times.time_id
    WHERE countries.country_name = 'France'
      AND promotions.promo_total_id = 1
      AND channels.channel_total_id = 1
      AND times.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
),

sales_agg AS (
    SELECT
        prod_id,
        year,
        month,
        SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY prod_id, year, month
),

sales_2019 AS (
    SELECT prod_id, month, total_sales AS sales_2019
    FROM sales_agg
    WHERE year = 2019
),

sales_2020 AS (
    SELECT prod_id, month, total_sales AS sales_2020
    FROM sales_agg
    WHERE year = 2020
),

projected_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        s20.prod_id,
        s20.month,
        s20.sales_2020,
        COALESCE(s19.sales_2019, 0) AS sales_2019,
        CASE 
            WHEN s19.sales_2019 = 0 THEN s20.sales_2020
            ELSE (((s20.sales_2020 - s19.sales_2019) * s20.sales_2020) / s19.sales_2019) + s20.sales_2020
        END AS projected_sales
    FROM sales_2020 s20
    LEFT JOIN sales_2019 s19 ON s20.prod_id = s19.prod_id AND s20.month = s19.month
),

currency_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        country AS country_name,
        year,
        month,
        to_us AS exchange_rate_to_usd
    FROM currency
    WHERE country = 'France' AND year = 2021
),

sales_2021_converted AS (
    SELECT
        p.month,
        p.projected_sales,
        c.exchange_rate_to_usd,
        (p.projected_sales * COALESCE(c.exchange_rate_to_usd, 1)) AS projected_sales_usd
    FROM projected_2021 p
    LEFT JOIN currency_2021 c ON p.month = c.month
)

SELECT
    month,
    ROUND(AVG(projected_sales_usd), 2) AS avg_projected_sales_usd
FROM sales_2021_converted
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

WITH converted_volume AS (
    SELECT
        ticker,
        date,
        CASE
            WHEN volume = '-' THEN 0
            WHEN volume LIKE '%M' THEN CAST(REPLACE(volume, 'M', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000000
            WHEN volume LIKE '%K' THEN CAST(REPLACE(volume, 'K', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000
            ELSE CAST(volume AS FLOAT)
        END AS volume_num
    FROM bitcoin_prices
    WHERE date BETWEEN '2021-08-01' AND '2021-08-10'
),
filtered_volume AS (
    SELECT
        ticker,
        date,
        volume_num
    FROM converted_volume
),
prev_nonzero_volume AS (
    SELECT
        cv1.ticker,
        cv1.date,
        cv1.volume_num,
        (SELECT volume_num
         FROM filtered_volume cv2
         WHERE cv2.ticker = cv1.ticker
           AND cv2.date < cv1.date
           AND cv2.volume_num > 0
         ORDER BY cv2.date DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS prev_volume_num
    FROM filtered_volume cv1
),
daily_pct_change AS (
    SELECT
        ticker,
        date,
        volume_num,
        prev_volume_num,
        CASE
            WHEN prev_volume_num IS NULL OR prev_volume_num = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE ((volume_num - prev_volume_num) / prev_volume_num) * 100
        END AS daily_volume_pct_change
    FROM prev_nonzero_volume
)
SELECT
    ticker,
    date,
    daily_volume_pct_change
FROM daily_pct_change
ORDER BY ticker, date;
```

WITH model_steps AS (
  SELECT
    m.name AS model_name,
    m.version AS model_version,
    ms.step,
    ms.l1_model,
    ms.is_stack,
    ms.test_score
  FROM model m
  JOIN model_score ms ON m.id = ms.model_id
),
step_max_scores AS (
  SELECT
    model_name,
    model_version,
    step,
    MAX(CASE WHEN is_stack = 0 THEN test_score ELSE NULL END) AS max_non_stack_score,
    MAX(CASE WHEN is_stack = 1 THEN test_score ELSE NULL END) AS stack_score
  FROM model_steps
  GROUP BY model_name, model_version, step
),
model_status AS (
  SELECT
    model_name,
    model_version,
    CASE 
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM step_max_scores AS s2
        WHERE s2.model_name = s1.model_name
          AND s2.model_version = s1.model_version
          AND s2.max_non_stack_score < s2.stack_score
      ) THEN 'strong'
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM step_max_scores AS s2
        WHERE s2.model_name = s1.model_name
          AND s2.model_version = s1.model_version
          AND s2.max_non_stack_score = s2.stack_score
      ) THEN 'soft'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS status
  FROM step_max_scores s1
  GROUP BY model_name, model_version
),
model_l1_status AS (
  SELECT
    ms.model_name,
    ms.model_version,
    ms.l1_model,
    ms.is_stack,
    ms.test_score,
    mstatus.status
  FROM model_steps ms
  JOIN model_status mstatus ON ms.model_name = mstatus.model_name AND ms.model_version = mstatus.model_version
  WHERE mstatus.status IS NOT NULL
),
l1_model_status_counts AS (
  SELECT

    l1_model,
    COUNT(*) AS occurrence

  GROUP BY status, l1_model
),

)

FROM l1_model_status_counts l
JOIN max_occurrences m ON l.status = m.status AND l.occurrence = m.max_occurrence
ORDER BY l.status;

WITH RECURSIVE
  -- Recursive CTE to find all nested packaging and accumulate quantities from bottom to top
  nested_packaging(parent_packaging_id, child_packaging_id, quantity) AS (
    SELECT packaging_id AS parent_packaging_id, child_packaging_id, quantity
    FROM packaging_relations
    UNION ALL
    SELECT np.parent_packaging_id, pr.child_packaging_id, pr.quantity * np.quantity
    FROM nested_packaging np
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON np.child_packaging_id = pr.parent_packaging_id
  ),

  -- Aggregate total quantity per top-level packaging and item
  item_quantities AS (
    SELECT
      p_top.packaging_id AS top_packaging_id,
      p_top.name AS top_packaging_name,
      pr.item_id,
      SUM(COALESCE(np.quantity, 1)) AS total_quantity -- multiply quantities down the chain. Use 1 for direct packaging.
    FROM packaging p_top
    LEFT JOIN nested_packaging np ON p_top.packaging_id = np.parent_packaging_id
    LEFT JOIN packaging_relations pr ON np.child_packaging_id = pr.parent_packaging_id
    OR (p_top.packaging_id = pr.parent_packaging_id AND np.child_packaging_id IS NULL)
    JOIN inventory i ON pr.item_id = i.item_id
    WHERE p_top.packaging_id NOT IN (SELECT child_packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
    GROUP BY p_top.packaging_id, p_top.name, pr.item_id
  )

SELECT
  ipq.top_packaging_name AS packaging_container_name,
  it.name AS item_name
FROM item_quantities ipq
JOIN products it ON ipq.item_id = it.product_id
WHERE ipq.total_quantity > 500
ORDER BY ipq.top_packaging_name, it.name;
```

    r.round,

  FROM results res

  WHERE r.year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959

    dsf.year,
    MIN(dsr.race_order) AS first_race_order,

  JOIN driver_season_races dsr ON dsf.driver_id = dsr.driver_id AND dsf.year = dsr.year
  GROUP BY dsf.driver_id, dsf.year

  FROM orderlines ol
  WHERE ol.order_id = 423
  ORDER BY ol.id

  FROM inventory i

  JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
  WHERE l.warehouse = 1

  ORDER BY i.product_id, p.purchased ASC, i.qty ASC
),

pick_plan AS (
  SELECT ol.line_id, ol.product_id, ol.quantity AS order_quantity, io.location_id, io.aisle, io.position, io.available_quantity,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ol.line_id) AS order_line_seq,
         SUM(ol.quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ol.line_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_order_qty

A legislator is considered retained if they are serving on December 31 of the respective year. Only include states where both gender cohorts maintain non-zero retention rates at all six of these time points during the first decade of service.

WITH gender_retention AS (
  SELECT
    state_abbreviation,
    gender,
    retention_year,
    COUNT(*) AS retained_legislators
  FROM (
    SELECT
      l.state_abbreviation,
      lt.gender,
      CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) AS start_year,
      -- Calculate retention year intervals 0,2,4,6,8,10
      CASE
        WHEN julianday('"' || (CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + 0) || '-12-31"') - julianday(lt.term_start_date) >= 0
          THEN 0
        WHEN julianday('"' || (CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + 2) || '-12-31"') - julianday(lt.term_start_date) >= 0
          THEN 2
        WHEN julianday('"' || (CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + 4) || '-12-31"') - julianday(lt.term_start_date) >= 0
          THEN 4
        WHEN julianday('"' || (CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + 6) || '-12-31"') - julianday(lt.term_start_date) >= 0
          THEN 6
        WHEN julianday('"' || (CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + 8) || '-12-31"') - julianday(lt.term_start_date) >= 0
          THEN 8
        WHEN julianday('"' || (CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + 10) || '-12-31"') - julianday(lt.term_start_date) >= 0
          THEN 10
        ELSE NULL
      END AS retention_year
    FROM legislators l
    JOIN legislators_terms lt ON l.id = lt.legislator_id
    WHERE lt.term_start_date IS NOT NULL
  )
  WHERE retention_year IN (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt2

        AND date(lt2.term_start_date, '+' || retention_year || ' years') <= date(CAST(strftime('%Y', lt.term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + retention_year || '-12-31')
    )
  GROUP BY state_abbreviation, gender, retention_year
),

retention_flags AS (
  SELECT
    state_abbreviation,
    gender,
    retention_year,
    CASE WHEN retained_legislators > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_retention
  FROM gender_retention
),

state_gender_retention AS (
  SELECT
    state_abbreviation,
    retention_year,
    SUM(CASE WHEN gender = 'M' THEN has_retention ELSE 0 END) AS male_retained,
    SUM(CASE WHEN gender = 'F' THEN has_retention ELSE 0 END) AS female_retained
  FROM retention_flags
  GROUP BY state_abbreviation, retention_year
),

states_all_intervals AS (
  SELECT
    state_abbreviation
  FROM state_gender_retention
  WHERE male_retained > 0
    AND female_retained > 0
  GROUP BY state_abbreviation
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT retention_year) = 6
)

WITH
-- Extract starting inventory as sum of qty in inventory for Dec 2018 per product
starting_inventory AS (
    SELECT i.product_id, SUM(i.qty) AS total_qty
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', p.purchased) = '2018-12'
    GROUP BY i.product_id
),

-- Minimum inventory per product
minimum_inventory AS (
    SELECT product_id, qty_minimum
    FROM product_minimums
),

-- Aggregate monthly purchases in 2019 per product
monthly_purchases AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           CAST(strftime('%m', purchased) AS INTEGER) AS month,
           SUM(qty) AS purchase_qty
    FROM purchases
    WHERE strftime('%Y', purchased) = '2019'
    GROUP BY product_id, month
),

-- Recursive inventory calculation month by month for 2019
inventory_2019 AS (
    -- Anchor: month = 1 (January 2019)
    SELECT 
        si.product_id,
        2019 AS year,
        1 AS month,
        CASE WHEN si.total_qty < pm.qty_minimum THEN pm.qty_minimum ELSE si.total_qty END AS start_inventory,
        CASE WHEN si.total_qty < pm.qty_minimum THEN pm.qty_minimum + COALESCE(mp.purchase_qty, 0) ELSE si.total_qty + COALESCE(mp.purchase_qty, 0) END AS end_inventory,
        pm.qty_minimum
    FROM starting_inventory si
    JOIN minimum_inventory pm ON si.product_id = pm.product_id
    LEFT JOIN monthly_purchases mp ON si.product_id = mp.product_id AND mp.month = 1

    UNION ALL

    -- Recursive step for months 2 to 12
    SELECT
        inv.product_id,
        2019 AS year,
        inv.month + 1 AS month,
        CASE WHEN inv.end_inventory < inv.qty_minimum THEN inv.qty_minimum ELSE inv.end_inventory END AS start_inventory,
        CASE WHEN inv.end_inventory < inv.qty_minimum THEN inv.qty_minimum + COALESCE(mp.purchase_qty, 0) ELSE inv.end_inventory + COALESCE(mp.purchase_qty, 0) END AS end_inventory,
        inv.qty_minimum
    FROM inventory_2019 inv
    LEFT JOIN monthly_purchases mp ON inv.product_id = mp.product_id AND mp.month = inv.month + 1
    WHERE inv.month < 12
)

SELECT product_id, month,
       ABS(end_inventory - qty_minimum) AS abs_difference
FROM (
    SELECT product_id, month, end_inventory, qty_minimum,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY ABS(end_inventory - qty_minimum)) AS rnk
    FROM inventory_2019
)
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY product_id;

Using a recursive monthly inventory adjustment model starting from December 2018 inventory levels, where we restock a product if its ending inventory drops below the minimum required level, determine for each product the month in 2019 where the absolute difference between its ending inventory and the minimum required level is the smallest, and return the product_id, that month, and the absolute difference.

WITH
-- Starting inventory at 2018-12 (December 2018) per product
starting_inventory AS (
    SELECT product_id, inventory_level AS end_inventory
    FROM inventory
    WHERE year = 2018 AND month = 12
),

-- Minimum inventory per product
minimum_inventory AS (
    SELECT product_id, minimum_inventory
    FROM product_minimums
),

-- Recursive month numbers for 2019
month_numbers AS (
    SELECT 1 AS m
    UNION ALL
    SELECT m + 1 FROM month_numbers WHERE m < 12
),

-- Calculate inventory month by month for 2019 recursively
inventory_2019 AS (
    -- Anchor: month 1 (January 2019) starting from December 2018
    SELECT 
        si.product_id,
        2019 AS year,
        1 AS month,
        -- Calculate starting inventory for Jan 2019 based on December 2018
        CASE 
            WHEN si.end_inventory < pm.minimum_inventory THEN pm.minimum_inventory
            ELSE si.end_inventory
        END AS start_inventory,
        -- Ending inventory for Jan = start_inventory since no sales data specified
        CASE 
            WHEN si.end_inventory < pm.minimum_inventory THEN pm.minimum_inventory
            ELSE si.end_inventory
        END AS end_inventory,
        pm.minimum_inventory
    FROM starting_inventory si
    JOIN minimum_inventory pm ON si.product_id = pm.product_id

    UNION ALL

    -- Recursive: for months 2 to 12
    SELECT 
        i.product_id,
        2019 AS year,
        i.month + 1 AS month,
        -- start_inventory is previous end_inventory unless below minimum
        CASE 
            WHEN i.end_inventory < i.minimum_inventory THEN i.minimum_inventory
            ELSE i.end_inventory
        END AS start_inventory,
        -- end_inventory same as start_inventory
        CASE 
            WHEN i.end_inventory < i.minimum_inventory THEN i.minimum_inventory
            ELSE i.end_inventory
        END AS end_inventory,
        i.minimum_inventory
    FROM inventory_2019 i
    WHERE i.month < 12
)

SELECT product_id, month,
       ABS(end_inventory - minimum_inventory) AS abs_difference
FROM (
    SELECT product_id, month, end_inventory, minimum_inventory,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY ABS(end_inventory - minimum_inventory)) AS rnk
    FROM inventory_2019
)
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY product_id;

WITH player_runs AS (
    SELECT 
        pm.player_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT pm.match_id) AS matches_played,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS total_runs
    FROM player_match pm
    JOIN batsman_scored bs ON pm.player_id = bs.batsman_id AND pm.match_id = bs.match_id
    JOIN match m ON pm.match_id = m.match_id
    WHERE m.season = 5
    GROUP BY pm.player_id
),
player_averages AS (
    SELECT 
        pr.player_id,
        pr.total_runs * 1.0 / pr.matches_played AS avg_runs_per_match
    FROM player_runs pr
    WHERE pr.matches_played > 0
),
batting_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        pm.player_id,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN wt.wicket_type IN ('bowled', 'caught', 'lbw', 'stumped', 'hit wicket') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS batting_average
    FROM player_match pm
    JOIN batsman_scored bs ON pm.player_id = bs.batsman_id AND pm.match_id = bs.match_id
    LEFT JOIN wicket_taken wt ON bs.match_id = wt.match_id AND bs.batsman_id = wt.player_out
    JOIN match m ON pm.match_id = m.match_id
    WHERE m.season = 5
    GROUP BY pm.player_id
)
SELECT p.player_name, pa.avg_runs_per_match, ba.batting_average
FROM player_averages pa
JOIN batting_avg ba ON pa.player_id = ba.player_id
JOIN player p ON pa.player_id = p.player_id
ORDER BY pa.avg_runs_per_match DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

WITH sales_with_year_week AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    week,
    sales_amount
  FROM weekly_sales
  WHERE year IN (2018, 2019, 2020)

  -- June 15 week number roughly around week 24 of each year (varies slightly by year, but we use 24 as approximate midpoint)
  SELECT DISTINCT year, 24 AS mid_week FROM sales_with_year_week

weekly_sales_lag_lead AS (
  SELECT
    s.year,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.week BETWEEN d.mid_week - 4 AND d.mid_week - 1 THEN s.sales_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.week BETWEEN d.mid_week AND d.mid_week + 3 THEN s.sales_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM sales_with_year_week s
  JOIN date_reference d ON s.year = d.year
  GROUP BY s.year
)
SELECT
  year,
  sales_before,
  sales_after,
  ROUND((CAST(sales_after AS FLOAT) - sales_before) / NULLIF(sales_before, 0) * 100, 2) AS pct_change
FROM weekly_sales_lag_lead
ORDER BY year;

  SELECT
    p.customer_id,
    p.payment_date,
    f.rating
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  WHERE (p.customer_id, p.payment_date) IN (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(payment_date)
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
  )
), 
CustomerRentals AS (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_rentals
  FROM rental r
  GROUP BY r.customer_id
),
JoinedData AS (
  SELECT
    fr.rating,
    fr.customer_id,
    SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount,
    (cr.total_rentals - 1) AS subsequent_rentals
  FROM FirstRental fr
  JOIN payment p ON fr.customer_id = p.customer_id
  JOIN CustomerRentals cr ON fr.customer_id = cr.customer_id
  GROUP BY fr.customer_id, fr.rating, cr.total_rentals
)
SELECT
  rating,
  AVG(total_amount) AS avg_total_amount_per_customer,
  AVG(subsequent_rentals) AS avg_subsequent_rentals_per_customer
FROM JoinedData
GROUP BY rating
